AI Boom Propels Samsung to Record 2Q26 Results as Operating Profit Surges 1,814% YoY  Samsung Electronics reported record-breaking results for the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure. The company posted consolidated revenue of ₩171.5T, up 130% YoY, while operating profit reached ₩89.5T, soaring 1,814% YoY. Both figures marked new quarterly records.. According to Samsung's financial results, the exceptional performance was driven almost entirely by the company's semiconductor business, underscoring the strong profitability of AI-related memory products.   hashtag #HBM4 and AIServer Demand Drive Semiconductor Growth  Samsung's Device Solutions (DS) division, which oversees its semiconductor operations, generated ₩127.5T in revenue and ₩89.2T in operating profit during the quarter.  According to the company's 2Q26 earnings presentation, the Memory Business recorded ₩120.8T in revenue, representing a 471% YoY increase and setting a new all-time high.  Samsung stated that, amid tight production capacity, it prioritized shipments to the server market, where continued memory price increases helped server products account for a record share of memory revenue. The company also significantly expanded shipments of HBM4 and delivered samples of the industry's first HBM4E to major customers, further reinforcing its technology leadership in next-generation AI memory.  In addition, Samsung's foundry business reported improved profitability, supported by strong orders from U.S. customers and growing demand for HBM base dies. The company also continued securing 2nm HPC design wins, strengthening its advanced foundry pipeline.   hashtag #Rising Component Costs Weighon Consumer Electronics  In contrast to the strong performance of the semiconductor business, Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division, which includes smartphones and consumer electronics, faced mounting cost pressures. Quarterly revenue declined 9% sequentially.  Within the DX division, the Mobile eXperience (MX) business reported ₩33.2T in revenue and an operating loss of ₩0.7T, primarily due to industry-wide increases in component costs that weighed on profitability.  TrendForce notes that while AI infrastructure investment continues to drive robust demand for high-value memory products such as HBM and server DRAM, rising component costs are increasingly pressuring consumer electronics manufacturers. AI Demand Continues to Surge as SK hynix Reports Record Revenue and Profit in 2Q26  SK hynix reported record-breaking results for the second quarter of FY2026, posting revenue of ₩79.318T, up 257% YoY. Operating profit reached ₩60.5426T, representing a 557% YoY increase, while net profit totaled ₩93.9226T. The company achieved an operating margin of 76% and a net margin of 118%, with both quarterly revenue and profit reaching all-time highs. Cumulative first-half revenue also exceeded ₩100T for the first time.  SK hynix attributed its strong performance to continued price increases for both DRAM and NAND Flash, alongside robust demand for high-value-added products, including HBM, AI server DRAM, and enterprise SSDs (eSSDs). As AI continues evolving toward Agentic AI and becomes increasingly integrated across a broad range of services, the company expects memory demand to broaden beyond AI-specific applications, creating a structural growth trend in both AI-oriented and mainstream memory markets.  On the DRAM front, SK hynix further strengthened its leadership in HBM. The company's HBM4, offering industry-leading power efficiency and cost competitiveness, entered mass production during the second quarter, with production scheduled to expand further in the second half of the year. Customer samples of HBM4E were also successfully delivered during the first half of 2026. Additionally, SOCAMM2, manufactured using the company's sixth-generation 10nm-class (1c) process technology, officially entered volume shipments and recorded strong sales growth during the quarter.  In the NAND Flash business, 321L QLC products have become the company's highest-volume NAND offering. SK hynix aims to increase the proportion of 321L QLC production at its Korean manufacturing facilities to approximately 50% by the end of 2026, further optimizing its product mix toward higher-performance, higher-value storage solutions.  TrendForce previously noted that major memory suppliers continue prioritizing capital expenditure toward DRAM expansion, leaving NAND Flash capacity additions relatively limited. As a result, NAND supply growth in 2026 has primarily been driven by process technology migration rather than significant capacity expansion, keeping market supply relatively tight without signs of substantial oversupply.   Looking ahead to 2027, suppliers in South Korea, the U.S., and Japan are expected to continue advancing process technologies while gradually bringing new capacity online. Meanwhile, Chinese manufacturers are projected to further expand production as additional equipment enters operation, with China's share of global NAND Flash supply expected to approach 19%. TrendForce expects the NAND Flash market to gradually rebalance in 2H27 as new capacity ramps throughout the industry, easing the current supply tightness.  📊 More semiconductor insights: https://buff.ly/4466Utg  📊 More industry charts: https://buff.ly/4hbxzLr

CEO Lip-Bu Tan described the quarter as Intel's strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years, highlighting that AI is driving unprecedented demand for computing.
